item.title: U.S. Trade Deficit Slipped To $901 Billion Last Year Amid Trump Tariffs
item.description: By PAUL WISEMAN AP Economics Writer WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. trade deficit slipped modestly in 2025, a year in which President Donald Trump upended global commerce by slapping double digit tariffs on imports from most countries. item.title: Early Prenatal Care, Considered Best For Moms And Babies, Is On The Decline In The US
item.description: By LAURA UNGAR AP Medical Writer Early prenatal care improves the chances of having a healthy pregnancy and baby. But a new federal report shows it’s been on the decline. The share of U.S. births to women who began prenatal care in the first trimester dropped from 78.3% in 2021 to 75.5% in 2024, according to data released by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Thursday. item.title: Bathroom Bill Tested
item.description: The newly-passed Texas Women’s Privacy Act is getting its first test. The parent of a child that goes to Austin High School has filed a complaint with the state Attorney General’s Office, saying a boy is being allowed to use the girl’s restroom. She’s backed by the group Texas Values, which says the law is clear. Public school students must use the restrooms according to their biological sex.

item.title: Judge Declares 4 Men Wrongly Accused Of 1991 Austin Yogurt Shop Murders Innocent
item.description: By JIM VERTUNO Associated Press AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — A Texas judge on Thursday declared four men who were wrongfully accused of the 1991 Austin yogurt shop murders innocent, formally clearing their names in a courtroom for the first time since the killings of four teenage girls that haunted the city for decades. “You are innocent,” state District Judge Dayna Blazey said during a hearing in a packed Austin courtroom.
